claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

This will help me assess your eligibility on a per-child basis.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm inquiring about my child, Alex. Just the one child - can you help me work out if I'm eligible?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Of course! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

To assess your eligibility, I need to gather some information about your circumstances. Let me start with the first question:

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 6 years old - born in 2018. Do you need the exact date?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. The year is helpful, so I have that Alex was born in 2018 and is currently 6 years old.

Let me continue with my next question:

**Are you living in the UK, and if so, what is your residency status?** (For example, are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or on a specific visa?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester actually. I'm a British citizen, have lived here all my life.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for that. That's helpful information.

Now, let me ask about your work and National Insurance contributions:

**Are you currently working, and if so, do you pay National Insurance contributions?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I work and pay National Insurance contributions like normal.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Let me ask one more important question:

**Are you currently receiving any of the following benefits: Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, income-related Employment and Support Allowance, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any of those benefits at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one more question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or training, or does Alex have any disabilities or health conditions that might be relevant?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is only 6, so just in primary school - normal schooling for their age.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the key facts:
- Alex is 6 years old (born in 2018)
- You are a British citizen living in the UK
- You are working and paying National Insurance contributions
- You are not receiving means-tested benefits
- Alex is in primary school with no relevant health conditions or disabilities

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you meet all the requirements. You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Congratulations! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.** 

You can now proceed with your claim if you haven't already done so. Is there anything else I can help you with regarding your eligibility?
